correctness.rationale: If a central element is decomposed homogeneously, bracketing with an element of either fixed degree separates the two summands by degree, so both are central even in characteristic two. In the even-center sector the quotient summands are orthogonal symplectic complements, with dimensions 2r and 2(m-r); the component avoiding the center has q^(2r) graph lifts. In the odd-center sector both quotient summands are isotropic, hence transverse Lagrangians, and there are q^m graph lifts. The corresponding symplectic stabilizers are Sp_(2r)×Sp_(2m-2r) and GL_m; symplectic lifts and central shears act transitively within sectors, with degree of center and odd dimension separating them. These arguments include r=0,m. The group orders give the stated exponents and exact counts. Writing r=m/2+t and S_j=q^(2j^2+j)P_j gives E/q^(m^2+m)=q^(2t-4t^2)P_m/(P_r P_(m-r)). At fixed t the ratio tends to 1/P_q and is bounded by P_q^(-2); extending by zero outside the support gives summable domination and normalized L1 convergence. Dividing by the odd-center count gives the rare-event constant. The reflection t↦1/2−t preserves the exponent and exchanges lattices, so the two theta sums are equal: parity changes the lattice law, not the leading rare-event prefactor. No inequality between the prefactors is asserted. Independent binary RREF subspace and bracket checks corroborate strata (1,4,12) and (1,80,16,480); these are finite checks only. The frozen checker and output provide a separate replay path in the source directory.

This is an automorphism-equivariant bijection. The indexed count at even-center rank 2r is q^(2r)S_m/(S_r S_(m-r)); the odd-center sector has rank m+1 and count q^(m+m(m+1)/2)∏(q^i+1). value.rationale: Uniform labeled gradings are a natural sampling model distinct from uniform orbit classes. The census shows an exponential preference for odd center as dimension grows; conditional on the rare sector, it identifies an order-one discrete fluctuation law rather than a broad Gaussian limit. The two parity cases describe shifted/reflected lattice distributions, not different leading probabilities. The value is this comparison and fluctuation scale, not the known orbit count or a recomputation of small cases.
